A1.justification: Both PDFs describe V2P-Bench, retaining the 980-video, 1,172-question benchmark and twelve evaluation dimensions. Their complete main texts, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original model, human and blind-answering evaluations in Tables 2–3, plus the Retrieval-versus-Needle experiment in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, a user study, controlled prompting experiments, error analyses and additional experiments in Appendices C and I.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds an auxiliary automated data-generation procedure combining RAM++ target extraction, SAM3 tracking and mask propagation, and model-generated QA synthesis. The central benchmark remains manually constructed; the PDFs do not demonstrate use of this new pipeline in the reported evaluations or introduce a new LVLM architecture.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation to interactive question creation, open-ended answering and mismatched video-question scenarios. Appendix I.3 also evaluates guessing behavior on MVBench, Video-MME and LongVideoBench as separate benchmarks. The original benchmark coverage remains; regrouping its twelve dimensions from five task families into three does not itself change coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated model set is substantially refreshed. v2 adds o1, Gemini-2.5-Pro, InternVL3, MiMo-VL, Qwen2.5-VL and 72B LLaVA variants, while removing comparisons with GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5 models, PLLaVA, VideoLLaMA2, ShareGPT4Video and older InternVL/Qwen variants. Blind-answering comparator membership also changes. LLaVA-NeXT and its INST-IT variant are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes several retained models' frame budgets to 128; LLaVA-NeXT and INST-IT instead change from 16 and 64 frames respectively to four. v2 introduces controlled prompt comparisons, user-study procedures, open-ended judging and refusal tests. Its reported construction protocol also replaces Gemini-1.5-Pro with Gemini-2.5-Pro and omits the visual-prompt filtering stage. These documented changes do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds standard-versus-doodle prompt tests, shuffled-input and abstention controls, MCQ-versus-open-ended analyses, extensive frame-sampling sensitivity tests, temporal-certificate analysis, prompt-type breakdowns and an analysis of 470 predictions with illustrated failures. Conversely, v1's 265-example Retrieval-versus-Needle experiment is removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Pearson correlation estimation for agreement between multiple-choice and open-ended evaluations, reporting coefficients of 0.95 and 0.98. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run variability for benchmark scores. The retained blind-filtering procedure still specifies two inference rounds.

E6.justification: Many benchmark results are replaced or added: v1's highest listed model is Gemini-1.5-Pro at 67.9%, while v2 newly reports o1 at 71.8%. LLaVA-Video-7B changes from 52.6% to 54.8% alongside a 64-to-128-frame setting change. Human performance remains 88.3% and GPT-4o remains 65.4%. User-study, refusal, open-ended, prompt-type and sampling results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, theorems or proofs. The task regrouping preserves the underlying dimension definitions, and v2's additional empirical measures are not accompanied by new mathematical derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion introduce pervasive 'Hack Phenomena', artificially inflated scores, and their dependence on video duration and sampling density as central findings. This substantially expands the paper's contribution beyond v1's benchmark introduction and model-performance assessment. The benchmark contribution and model–human performance-gap claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations linking guessing to instruction-following pressure and insufficient visual information, explaining different frame-count effects across tasks, and attributing INST-IT's uneven transfer to prompt specialization and annotation format. It also argues for open-ended evaluation's resistance to guessing and discusses text-versus-visual dataset bias. The existing offline-only and no-audio limitations are retained in Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 supplies detailed annotation and distractor guidelines, filtering counts, exact inference and abstention prompts, VLMEvalKit guidance, human-scoring procedures and the Gradio/MS Paint user-study workflow. It newly states that data, evaluation scripts and a leaderboard have been released. Conversely, v1's explicit project URL and eight-V100 hardware disclosure disappear; external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work framework is largely retained, with targeted additions including o1, InternVL3, MiMo-VL, VLMEvalKit, SAM3 and Recognize Anything, and removal of several older model references. v2 sharpens its positioning against INST-IT and VideoRefer by emphasizing the interaction burden of annotating every frame, supplementing v1's existing diversity and duration criticisms.

P1.justification: The abstract, experimental discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten around explicit research questions and findings. Benchmark statistics and limitations move into appendices, the appendix organization expands from A–B to A–J, and five task-family headings become three while preserving twelve dimensions. These changes substantially restructure the narrative beyond simply inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout, redraws Figure 1, adds a human trace to the radar chart, consolidates selected appendix examples into main-text Figure 4, and rearranges the relocated distribution plots. Numerous comparison tables, diagnostic plots and annotated failure figures are added, while the original Retrieval-versus-Needle plot is removed.

improvement.justification: The new user study, controlled diagnostic experiments and detailed prompts and annotation instructions improve the empirical grounding, interpretability and reproducibility of v1. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 3a gives Qwen2.5-VL-7B 52.4% versus 48.1% in Table 2 without explaining different conditions, and Table 3b reports visual-prompt satisfaction of 7.5 while the text claims 8.2. These contradictions weaken confidence in important new findings despite the useful additions.
